quick.summary: Why building for massive future growth today is a costly mistake.
quick.takeaway: Design for the next two years, not the next ten.

beats.line: I am building a pipeline for ten users. Should I make it handle millions?
If you need to drive to work alone, do you buy a city bus?
No, that would be incredibly slow to park and expensive to run.
Exactly. Building for massive scale too early slows you down and costs a fortune.
Can I just call it over building?
Choose a simple design that works for the next two years. Then rethink it.
I will stick to a basic script until we get more than fifty users.
Your future self will thank you for keeping it simple today.

quiz.question: You are creating a tool for a team of five people. What is the best approach?
options: Build the simplest solution that handles their current needs.
Buy a massive server cluster just in case the company grows.
Spend six months designing a system for global traffic.
Refuse to build it until there are thousands of users.
quiz.explanation: Over building wastes time and money. Solve the problem you have today with a design that lasts a year or two.

quiz.question: A simple design cannot be rethought or changed later.
quiz.explanation: You can always rethink a design when you outgrow it. A simple system is often easier to replace.
